meta.type: WordPress child theme of hex-wp-theme-template (Hexnity WP AI Theme)
meta.purpose: Child theme that inherits all templates from its parent via WordPress's normal template hierarchy, and owns the theme-options.css data file the parent's Theme Options admin page writes to. Does NOT own a Tailwind build of its own (reversed 2026-08-29, see action-map.json) — the admin-configurable design-system CSS build lives and compiles in the parent theme only; this child theme keeps a reference-only, unbuilt copy of site-theme.css for a child developer to read/adapt.
meta.boundary: All work is strictly confined to this child theme's own directory — do not reach into the parent theme's directory. See claude.md and GUIDELINES.md.

docs.claude.md: Session entry point — process rules for working in this directory (read GUIDELINES.md next, read TEMPLATE-CONVERSION-GUIDE.md too if the task touches the HTML-to-template workflow, bootstrap/maintain this project.json + action-map.json, versioning, folder boundary).
docs.GUIDELINES.md: The compatibility contract with the parent theme — required style.css header, enqueue architecture, theme-options.css format rules (always px, derived/reserved keys, custom-token auto-detection), why not to redefine the parent's former class names now owned here, independent-updater isolation, versioning, folder boundary, (§8, added 2026-08-29) the convention for using the parent's Page Content JSON framework when building/converting a page template here, and (§9, added 2026-08-30) this child theme's own branded header/footer (header.php/footer.php + template-parts/site-header.php/site-footer.php) driven by the parent's sibling Site Content JSON framework.
docs.TEMPLATE-CONVERSION-GUIDE.md: Living, purely-prescriptive reference for converting an HTML/CSS concept file (theme root) into a WordPress page template using this theme's real design-token system: how to map every value onto theme-options.css fields, why every font-size must use one of the theme's 11 existing .hex-* fluid classes (never hardcoded, never a hand-written clamp()), why every font-family must come from the 4 real --hex-font-* fields via .font-accent/.font-mono, why var(--hex-spacing-x, mismatched-fallback) silently renders the wrong value, how to reuse the parent's real component classes (.btn/.card/.badge/.form-control/.nav-link/.icon) before authoring anything new, why site-theme.css is now the ONLY CSS file (directly enqueued, no separate mirror, unconditionally loaded on every page as of 2026-08-30), why every piece of editor-facing text must come from hex_get_page_content() (GUIDELINES.md §8) rather than being hardcoded, and (rule 9 / step 9) why wiring a template to that framework is not enough on its own -- the default JSON must also actually be saved to the database (hex_save_page_content()) for every live Page assigned that template, checked as a standing invariant any time the template's content is touched, not just once at conversion time. As of 2026-08-30 also documents (rule 10 / step 10) that every template calls get_header()/get_footer() rather than rendering its own inline header/footer -- this theme's own branded global chrome (header.php/footer.php + template-parts/site-header.php/site-footer.php) -- and that header/footer text comes from a separate, site-wide Site Content JSON framework (hex_get_site_content(), GUIDELINES.md §9), never a page's own Page Content JSON, with the same wired-vs-backfilled invariant applying there too (against hex_save_site_content() and the 'primary' nav menu instead of a page ID). Also holds the current template inventory (one row per converted template, with a DB-backfill-status column separate from the wired-to-framework column). Update it after every task in this workflow -- see its own 'Keeping this guide current' section. Contains no mistake-narrative by design; that lives in action-map.json.

structure.style.css: Theme header (Template: hex-wp-theme-template) + a short comment pointing to the real styling location (the parent theme). Intentionally near-empty otherwise.
structure.functions.php: Enqueues this theme's own plain style.css (get_stylesheet_uri()), dependent on the parent's hex-tailwind handle for correct load order. No Tailwind BUILD pipeline of its own (no npm/package.json) -- but as of 2026-08-29 DOES directly enqueue assets/css/src/site-theme.css itself, since that file was rewritten to plain browser-native CSS that day. Originally conditional on is_page_template(array('template-home.php', 'template-ai-technology.php')); broadened to unconditional 2026-08-30 once header.php/footer.php made those classes global site chrome (see the header.php entry below). Also unconditionally enqueues Google Fonts for the sitewide --hex-font-heading ('Instrument Serif') and --hex-font-body ('Inter') Theme Options values, and (now also unconditionally, same 2026-08-30 change) 'IBM Plex Mono' for --hex-font-mono. Loads style.css a second time on purpose (the parent's own 'hex-style' handle already loads it once, early); do not deregister 'hex-style' from here -- confirmed live to break hex-animate/hex-tailwind, which both declare it as a dependency. See ../hex-wp-theme-template/knoladge/child-theme-css-token-architecture.md. Also (added 2026-08-30) hexnity_wp_child_cf7_disable_autop(), hooked to Contact Form 7's wpcf7_autop_or_not filter -- disables CF7's default wpautop() pass on its form-tag templates sitewide, so template-contact.php's embedded CF7 form renders with the exact markup shape site-theme.css's .form-split/.form-row-split expect (see GUIDELINES.md §10 and the template-contact.php entry below). Also (added 2026-09-01) hexnity_wp_child_enqueue_animation(), enqueuing this theme's own new assets/js/site-animate.js (no dependency, loaded in the footer) -- see that file's entry below. Also (added 2026-09-01, per explicit user report that assigning a template to a Page generated no JSON) hexnity_wp_child_get_template_defaults( $template_slug ) -- a switch-case registry holding the default Page Content payload for every one of this theme's 7 templates (template-broadband.php/-services.php/-our-brands.php/-results.php/-contact.php/-ai-technology.php/-home.php), each a straight transcription of that template's own hardcoded `??` fallback copy -- and hexnity_wp_child_maybe_backfill_page_content( $post_id, $post ), hooked to save_post_page at priority 20, which calls hex_save_page_content( $post_id, $defaults ) the moment a Page is saved with one of these templates assigned AND hex_get_page_content( $post_id ) is still empty (idempotent -- never overwrites a page that already has any saved content, including one this same hook already backfilled). Verified live against the real DB (a throwaway draft test page created, assigned a template via wp_update_post(), checked, mutated, resaved, and deleted, all in a temp script -- see action-map.json): JSON auto-generates on template assignment, two pages sharing the same template get fully independent rows, and re-saving an already-backfilled page never wipes an editor's own edits. Also confirmed via a separate throwaway-page test that hex_save_page_content()'s internal sanitization preserves a `class` attribute on inline HTML (e.g. `<span class="accent-text">`) through a full save/read round trip, before relying on that for the registry's several wp_kses_post()-rendered heading fields. UPDATED 2026-09-01: added hexnity_wp_child_setup() (after_setup_theme -> add_theme_support("custom-logo")) and hexnity_wp_child_get_site_logo( $section_content, $fallback_url ), a shared helper used by both site-header.php and site-footer.php to resolve the logo image in priority order: that section's own Site Content logo_url override, then the site's own Customizer "Site Identity" logo (custom_logo theme_mod -- per-site DB data, works on any site running this theme with no manual step), then the theme's bundled placeholder SVG. Added after an explicit user correction against an earlier session action that had hand-written a logo_url straight into one site's Site Content DB row -- a fix that would not have generalized to any other site running this same theme. UPDATED 2026-09-01: added hexnity_wp_child_maybe_backfill_site_content() (admin_init), the Site Content (header/footer) equivalent of hexnity_wp_child_maybe_backfill_page_content() -- idempotent, fills the header/footer Site Content JSON with this theme's original default copy only if that section is genuinely empty (a fresh site, or a site whose "Header & Footer" admin page was never saved), never overwrites existing content. Added because a theme code update (this theme's GitHub updater) only ships files, never database content -- across multiple sites running this theme, this makes the header/footer JSON self-create with sane defaults automatically on any site, rather than needing a manual per-site script or admin JSON paste. Deliberately excludes logo_url/logo_alt (left for hexnity_wp_child_get_site_logo()'s Customizer fallback) and the footer's columns/bottom_links (already covered by site-footer.php's own PHP-level fallback array).

structure.assets/js/site-animate.js: Added 2026-09-01, per explicit user request to add animations to all templates. Plain, hand-written, browser-native JS -- no build step, same approach as site-theme.css. A single self-invoking IIFE: bails out immediately if the visitor has prefers-reduced-motion set; otherwise, on DOMContentLoaded, selects every element matching a fixed list of bare structural selectors that already exist in every template (section, .hero, .page-hero, .brand-intro, .card, .path-card, .sec-head, .form-split, .compliance-box, .quote-block, .accordion-item, .stats-grid > div) -- deliberately NOT per-template classes, so this reaches every template (including template-home.php/template-ai-technology.php, which render without a <main> wrapper) with zero template markup edits. Adds .hex-anim-ready to <html> only once it has real targets, then .hex-reveal to each target and observes it with an IntersectionObserver (threshold 0.12, rootMargin '0px 0px -8% 0px'); adds .hex-in-view (and unobserves) the first time each element enters the viewport. Falls back to marking everything .hex-in-view immediately if IntersectionObserver isn't supported. Progressive enhancement is the load-bearing design constraint here: the actual hide/reveal CSS (site-theme.css's `.hex-anim-ready .hex-reveal` rules) is scoped under `.hex-anim-ready`, which this script is the only thing that ever adds -- so content stays fully visible with JS off, blocked, or erroring, and for reduced-motion visitors. Enqueued by hexnity_wp_child_enqueue_animation() in functions.php, footer-loaded, no dependency.

Its own inline <header>/<footer> blocks, the surrounding <!DOCTYPE html>/<head>/<body> boilerplate, and the now-unused $nav_links/$footer_columns/$footer_bottom_links Page Content fallback arrays were all removed; $content['site']['phone']/['email'] stay (read independently by the Contact section, unrelated to the header/footer). Every remaining component uses a real class -- the parent's existing .btn/.btn-primary/.btn-ghost/.card/.badge/.badge-outline/.badge-mono/.form-control/.form-label/.nav-menu/.nav-link/.icon, the theme's 11 real fluid text-size classes (.hex-h1...hex-h6/.hex-lead/.hex-small/.hex-meta), the .font-accent/.font-mono font-family utilities, plus the new layout classes -- all authored directly in assets/css/src/site-theme.css, this theme's own directly-enqueued CSS file. No inline <style> block, no inline style="" attributes, no hardcoded font-size or font-family anywhere, no other CSS file used or needed. Verified live (php -l, and curling the rendered page) after the 2026-08-30 split -- single <header>/<footer>/<!DOCTYPE>, zero PHP warnings, zero double-encoding. Renamed from template-meridian-home.php to template-home.php by the user on 2026-08-29; functions.php's is_page_template() check updated to match. Assign it to a Page via the editor's Template dropdown (and set that Page as the site's static front page in Settings > Reading to use it as the home page); the "Page Content (JSON)" meta box on that Page's Edit screen is where an editor customizes this page's own copy, and wp-admin's "Header & Footer" page (Site Content JSON, GUIDELINES.md §9) is where the header/footer are now customized instead.

Section order: a centered `.brand-intro` band (new component, see site-theme.css entry below) with a logo `` (defaults to assets/images/brand-more-logo.svg, this theme's own new placeholder asset) + a short blurb; a `.sec-head` + `.step-cards` 3-step 'Compare / Switch / Save' process (originally built with `.rows`/`.row-item` reused from template-services.php's row component, replaced 2026-09-01 with a new one-row 3-up `.card`-based grid per explicit user request to show the steps as cards in one row -- see the site-theme.css entry below), each card carrying a hand-drawn inline-SVG icon (compare/switch/save, `.icon.icon-lg` in a `.step-card-icon` circle) from a fixed `$step_icons` array keyed by position, per a further explicit request for icons (not emoji) -- hardcoded outside hex_get_page_content() since the icon is tied to the step's fixed real-world meaning, same pattern as the fixed phone/email/address icons on the Contact section; two `.sec-head`-only copy sections (`about` -- about the More brand, `usage` -- why to switch with it), the same heading+lede pattern template-home.php's Services/Results/Brands sections use, no new CSS; a Contact Form 7 enquiry form reusing template-contact.php's exact `.form-split` card pattern and the same sitewide form (id 41) via `contact.cf7_form_id ?? 41`; and an FAQ section using the parent's existing `.accordion`/`.accordion-item`/`.accordion-content` CSS-only component (already shipped in site-theme.css, not previously used by any template in this theme). hex_get_page_content() keys: `brand` (logo_url/logo_alt/blurb), `steps` (eyebrow/heading/items[num,title,desc]), `about` (eyebrow/heading/lede), `usage` (eyebrow/heading/lede), `contact` (eyebrow/heading/text/cf7_form_id), `site` (phone/email, read independently the same way template-contact.php's own Contact section does), `faq` (heading/items[question,answer]). Verified: php -l clean, brace-balanced CSS, mock-rendered with an empty $content array (zero PHP warnings, every fallback renders), and a classes-used-vs-classes-defined cross-check found zero orphaned classes. Assigned to Page ID 46 ("More"), published at /more/; content backfilled 2026-09-01 (hex_save_page_content()) once the user confirmed the page existed, including the real brand.logo_url this time (get_stylesheet_directory_uri() resolved against the live site, http://mindlabz-new.local). Not yet linked from the primary nav menu or footer columns (out of scope for this task, left for the user/editor). UPDATED 2026-09-01 (later the same day): this manual, one-off backfill process was replaced with an automatic one -- any Page (this one or a future one) assigned template-broadband.php now gets its own default JSON the moment it's saved, via hexnity_wp_child_maybe_backfill_page_content() in functions.php; see that entry and action-map.json.

structure.template-contact.php: WordPress Page Template (`Template Name: Contact`), added 2026-08-30 -- NOT standalone: get_header()/get_footer(). Extracted from template-home.php's "Contact" section (`#contact`). `.page-hero`/`.breadcrumb` (no CTA button in the hero -- the form is right below it, a second CTA would be redundant) + the exact `.form-split` markup/copy inside `<main id="primary">`. hex_get_page_content() keys: `hero` (breadcrumb_label/heading/lede only, no cta_label/cta_url), `site` (phone/email/address, read independently the same way template-home.php's own Contact section does -- not from the Site Content header/footer framework, which is a separate store per TEMPLATE-CONVERSION-GUIDE.md step 10), `contact` (eyebrow/heading/text -- `form_options`/`submit_label`/`fine_print` no longer read as of the same day's later update, see below). Verified the same way as template-services.php. Assigned to Page ID 40 ("Contact"), published, content backfilled the same day. UPDATED later 2026-08-30: the form itself is now a real Contact Form 7 form (`do_shortcode('[contact-form-7 id="41"...]')`, guarded by `class_exists('WPCF7_ContactForm')`, form ID read from `contact.cf7_form_id ?? 41`) instead of the original static non-functional `<form>` -- see GUIDELINES.md §10 for the full pattern (class: options on every CF7 field-tag matching real theme classes, the sitewide wpautop-disable filter, why CF7's own `<div class="wpcf7">` wrapper doesn't break `.form-split`'s CSS Grid). The now-unused `$contact_form_options` variable was removed -- the dropdown's own options live in CF7's form editor now, not this page's JSON.
